title: 'Unlock Your Price' price-reveal could not be confirmed free of personal-information collection
quote: *On approved credit. Payment does not reflect or include Sales Tax or Fees. See Dealer for full details. Expires Unlock Your Price
recommendation: **NEEDS HUMAN REVIEW AND VERIFICATION** — This is NOT an asserted violation. The VDP selling price sits behind an “Unlock Your Price” control, and the crawl returned has_price_gating = false and could not confirm whether that control simply reveals the price on click or first requires email/phone submission. If it reveals the price without collecting personal information, no CCPA financial-incentive disclosure is required and no action is needed. A reviewer should manually click “Unlock Your Price” on a live VDP and confirm whether PI is demanded before the price displays. (Site privacy posture is otherwise strong: full ComplyAuto CCPA/CPRA privacy center, GPC honored, cookie banner present.)

title: Used inventory pages do not reference the forthcoming CARS Act 3-day cancellation right
quote: 38 Used cars, trucks, and SUVs in Stock serving Costa Mesa, Lake Forest & Mission Viejo, CA
recommendation: **NEEDS HUMAN REVIEW AND VERIFICATION** — Best-practice advisory, not a current violation. The CARS Act 3-day cancellation right (used vehicles $50,000 or less) is not operative until October 1, 2026, and the statute's primary disclosure occurs at point of sale, so its absence from the website today is not itself a violation. No contradictory “all sales final” or rights-waiver language was detected in the captured used-inventory content (the VDP “Subject to prior sale” language is not a waiver). The automated crawl did not capture the full Terms of Service / purchase-policy pages, so any buried waiver language could not be checked. Recommend adding an accurate reference to the 3-day cancellation right on used VLP/VDP pages before the Oct. 1, 2026 operative date and reviewing site terms for any anti-cancellation language.

title: Unsubstantiated '#1 Rated' superlative ranking claim in the site-wide header
quote: OC's #1 Rated Nissan Dealer on Google
recommendation: **NEEDS HUMAN REVIEW AND VERIFICATION** — The header carries “OC's #1 Rated Nissan Dealer on Google” on every page. Unlike puffery, “#1 Rated” is a measurable, verifiable ranking/superlative that requires substantiation under B&P §17508, and Nissan BAP guidelines (NISSAN-PROHIB-001) prohibit unsubstantiated superlatives in Nissan advertising. The claim cites Google as a source, which is partial support, so this may be substantiable. A reviewer should confirm the dealer holds documented proof (e.g., highest average Google rating among Orange County Nissan dealers, with methodology and date) and ideally surface that basis near the claim; otherwise soften to non-comparative language. The automated audit cannot verify the underlying rating data.
